item: The vLLM start tests no longer depend on port 8001 being free, and the port-collision tests no longer hold it
summary: test_the_refusal_is_acknowledgeable failed on #1860's shard 2 (head f3875adce) with VllmLifecycleError: port 8001 is already taken by another server, which is not vLLM. Two tests in test_vllm_port_collision.py ran a real non-vLLM HTTP server on vLLM's default port (8001), while every start() test probes that same real port before it spawns (6 in test_vllm_start_diagnosable.py, 5 in test_vllm_lifecycle.py, 5 in test_gpu_arbitration.py) and none stubbed it. All four files are in shard 2, which runs them on parallel workers (-n auto --dist loadfile), so the two kinds overlapped and production code correctly refused a taken port. Reproduced by holding 127.0.0.1:8001 with a plain HTTP server: those 16 tests fail with the CI message. Now the collision tests bind a port the kernel picks and point OO_VLLM_URL at it (the free-port test still checks that with no override the probe reads the derived port), and the start() fixtures stub port_occupant as free, since the port refusal is the collision file's subject. With 8001 held, the four files pass (221). Release-notes line (R319): internal, users see no change.
